$comparability.why: A label is a judgement about a sentence, not about a build. These verdicts are still judgements about these sentences and node eval/apply-labels.mjs carries them forward, so the labels survive the golden set being rebuilt.
$comparability.carry_key_changed: The carry key is now (rfc, kind, text) rather than (rfc, text). One key in this set of files already carried both verdicts - rfc 7872, TRUE as a requirement and FALSE as a candidate - and the old key stored the contradiction silently. apply-labels.mjs now reports it instead of overwriting it.

notes: The carried 53 are all rows the BEFORE pass judged false and that are still present - mostly boilerplate, plus sentences phrased as list rows. They are kept in the denominator; a carried TRUE would need the flat `labels` form, which the BEFORE candidate file does not use, so carried precision reads 0% and only the false side carries.
after-CAND041, 043, 051, 052, 068, 137, 140, 143, 145, 146, 172 are the two unfiltered boilerplate families: 11 of 185 rows, 5.9%.

after-CAND004, 006, 005, 008, 020, 029, 037, 078, 089, 123, 133, 136, 149 are notation that survived into the candidate list - ABNF, ASN.1, a field table, an IANA template, an ASCII diagram, or a sentence the splitter cut mid-clause.

after-CAND173, 049, 081, 088, 144, 169, 171 carry `keyword: Required` taken from inside a quoted status name ('Length Required', 'Proxy Authentication Required', 'Specification Required'). The sentences carry a real MUST or SHOULD, so they are true positives filed under a keyword with no force there.
